title: api: schema versioning, beta headers, and backward-compat shims for openai-compat
author: Riley Gomez
description:
Motivation: We are rolling out the API schema v2 to support structured outputs, improved tool/function-calling, and clearer streaming semantics. To avoid breaking existing integrations (including the OpenAI compatibility layer), this PR introduces an explicit API versioning header, a beta feature header, and server-side backward-compatibility shims that translate v2 responses to v1 shapes when requested.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds X-Redwood-API-Version header parsing and enforcement on the API gateway and at internal handlers. Default remains v1 for unversioned requests.
- Adds X-Redwood-Beta header to opt into beta behaviors (e.g. structured output and stricter function-calling semantics).
- Implements server-side back-compat shims in openai-compat so that existing OpenAI-compatible clients keep receiving the v1 response schema even when the model/runtime produces v2 structured outputs.
- Updates the OpenAI compatibility adapter to negotiate version headers with Redwood runtime and to prefer explicit version headers over inferred behavior.
- Exposes a feature flag and an /internal/experimental/compat endpoint (restricted) for dogfooding and canarying the behavior.
- Adds unit and integration tests covering header precedence, shim correctness, streaming fallback behavior, and SDK header propagation.
- Docs: adds API versioning and migration guide, and updates SDK quickstarts to show how to opt in to v2/beta headers.

Checklist:
- [x] Gateway header parsing and validation implemented
- [x] openai-compat shims for response translation implemented
- [x] SDK propagation (Python/TS) updated to send explicit headers when requested
- [x] Tests added for v1->v2 & v2->v1 translation, streaming edge cases
- [x] Docs and release notes drafted

Compatibility notes: The runtime will default to v1 semantics unless callers set X-Redwood-API-Version: v2 or X-Redwood-Beta: structured-output. When v2 is selected, the server will produce structured outputs by default. For OpenAI-compatible endpoints we add a compatibility shim layer that rewrites structured outputs into the classic text/choices array shape for clients that do not opt in. This shim preserves tokenization and streaming partials where possible; in streaming scenarios the shim may buffer a small number of events to produce coherent v1 chunks (see performance note).

Performance note: the compatibility shim adds a small CPU overhead (~0.4ms/request in our bench) and can increase memory use for long structured responses during streaming. We added a runtime config to enable streaming passthrough for endpoints that can handle v2 shapes, and the default shim is enabled only for the openai-compat route to minimize impact to the main API path.

Backports/hotfix: none required for release branches. We landed this on main behind feature flags so we can canary via Internal feature endpoint and progressively enable by customer.

Related: ENG-4321 (schema v2 launch plan), ENG-4398 (openai-compat migration)

review_comments: Asha Patel (2026-01-12): Can we clarify header precedence? If both X-Redwood-API-Version and X-Redwood-Beta are present which one wins? Also request that gateway reject unknown version tokens with 400 instead of 500.

Riley Gomez (2026-01-12): Answered: X-Redwood-API-Version takes precedence. X-Redwood-Beta is additive and only enables opt-in beta features. Updated gateway to return 400 for unknown versions and added tests.

Marco Liu (2026-01-14): Performance microbench results look fine, but please add a toggle to disable shim buffering for low-latency customers. Request: expose config via runtime flags and document tradeoffs.
Riley Gomez (2026-01-15): Added runtime flag 'compat.stream_passthrough' and documented tradeoffs in versioning.md. Also wired flag into canary endpoint.

Add X-Redwood-Beta header to opt into beta features like structured output and stricter function-calling semantics.
